definitions.delta: Brier(method) minus Brier(reference) within the same cohort, predictor, budget and allocation; positive is worse.
definitions.harm: Proportion of 300 allocations with signed paired delta > 0; exact ties are retained and are not harmful. This is probability-prediction error, not a clinical-harm endpoint.
definitions.interval: Empirical 5th and 95th percentiles of 300 paired allocation differences, using linear interpolation; an allocation distribution, not a patient/population confidence interval.
definitions.worst10: Mean of the largest 30 signed paired allocation differences among 300 allocations. Negative differences remain negative; no truncation at zero. After excluding the first 20, average the largest 28 of 280.
definitions.average: Compute each predictor-specific Brier score separately; average the three scores equally within each allocation before forming allocation summaries. This is not an ensemble prediction model.
definitions.units: Mean Brier is unscaled. Delta means, allocation interval and worst-decile mean are displayed in units of 10^-3 (raw delta multiplied by 1000). Harm and selection frequencies are percentages.
definitions.remaining: Primary evaluation uses all patients outside the calibration sample: main n=555,1878,54.
definitions.common: Sensitivity/figure uses patients after each cohort largest calibration prefix: n=455,1778,54; held fixed across budgets within a repeat, varies between repeats.
definitions.table3: Method-selection percentages pool 900 predictor-specific decisions per cohort (300 allocations x 3 predictors). They do not describe one ensemble-level decision.
definitions.pilot: Exclusion of the original 20 allocations is a numerical diagnostic. The remaining 280 allocations reuse the same patients and do not remove historical/pilot-based study selection.
